purpose: Promote the first source-anchor backfill into field-level Source Cards for the highest-leverage falsifier families, so strong Human Infra claims can be reviewed by exact source identity, domain mapping, model position, supported use, transfer boundary and next extraction step.

scope.selectionRule: Select sources that anchor the largest number of model-critical falsifiers: aging mechanism taxonomy, biomarker versus endpoint, reprogramming identity risk, survival/hazard methods, causal intervention design, prediction reporting and subject-continuity value framing.
currentLimitations: This extraction covers the first 10 highest-leverage source anchors, not all 21 source anchors in the backfill register.
This extraction records field-level use and transfer boundaries; it is not a live external literature review.
This extraction does not validate intervention efficacy, individual medical action, individual lifespan, NCG calibration or personal prediction.
Remaining source anchors still require equivalent field-level extraction before RESEARCH-G6 can pass completely.

sourceIdentity.title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source as the high-level aging-mechanism scaffold for mapping Human Infra biological source-maintenance domains into variable families.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Mechanism taxonomy only; do not infer that any intervention extends lifespan or healthspan.

modelPosition.stateTransition: Mechanism hypotheses for how state deterioration could progress.
modelPosition.hazard: Indirect hazard vocabulary only; no source-specific hazard ratio is imported.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Suggests which biomarker or functional domains may need observation.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Supports healthspan and lifespan language only as conceptual targets.
modelPosition.optionValue: Supports the idea that multiple maintenance failures can constrain future action.

keyExtracts: Aging should be treated as a multi-hallmark system rather than a single variable.
Human Infra domain rows should separate mechanism plausibility from intervention outcome evidence.
Any strong longevity claim must identify which maintenance layer it affects and which layers remain unaddressed.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to group C2 source-maintenance domains and to require multi-mechanism downgrade conditions.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a claim treats one hallmark or one biomarker as sufficient for effective immortality, downgrade it to a narrow candidate mechanism.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not support individual prediction, clinical recommendation, intervention ranking or proof of longevity escape velocity.
risksAndMisreadings: Hallmark coverage can be mistaken for causality.
Mechanism breadth can be mistaken for therapeutic maturity.
Review-level synthesis can hide domain-specific uncertainty.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a shared source card for C2 mechanism taxonomy and RESEARCH-G3/G6 downgrade checks.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Split each hallmark used by a C2 domain into domain-level variable rows with endpoint, population and uncertainty fields.

sourceIdentity.title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to anchor biological-age clocks as observation and risk-association tools, not as proof that changing a clock changes survival.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Biomarker association is not an intervention effect.

modelPosition.stateTransition: No causal transition imported without intervention evidence.
modelPosition.hazard: Supports risk-association framing for mortality-related modeling.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Primary use: an observation layer candidate.
modelPosition.actionPolicy: Cannot directly select an action from the clock value.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Can inform aggregate lifespan/healthspan risk discussions only.
modelPosition.optionValue: May help prioritize uncertainty reduction if validated for the target population.

keyExtracts: A molecular clock can be useful for risk stratification without proving causal control.
Biomarker improvement must remain separate from disease endpoint or mortality improvement.
Model cards should report whether a variable is an observation proxy or an actionable mediator.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to force a biomarker-versus-endpoint distinction in longevity and model visualization claims.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a page treats a lower biological-age score as sufficient evidence of extended effective life, downgrade the claim.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not validate a personal prognosis, therapeutic target, lifespan extension intervention or calibrated Human Infra model.
risksAndMisreadings: Clock age can be overread as biological destiny.
Clock reversal can be overread as hazard reversal.
Population associations may not transfer to an individual or new cohort.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as the first field-level card for biological-age observation and no-individual-prediction boundaries.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Create a biomarker endpoint table separating clock inputs, outcome associations, target population and intervention evidence.

sourceIdentity.title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from mouse embryonic and adult fibroblast cultures by defined factors

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source as the origin anchor for defined-factor cellular identity reprogramming and the need to separate age reset from identity preservation.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Cellular reprogramming origin evidence is not whole-body rejuvenation evidence.

modelPosition.stateTransition: Defined factors can move cells toward pluripotent states under experimental conditions.
modelPosition.hazard: Risk language concerns identity loss and tumor-related safety gates, not quantified Human Infra hazard.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Requires markers that distinguish identity, age state and function.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Does not directly support lifespan, healthspan or effective-time estimates.
modelPosition.optionValue: Creates a research path for future repair technologies, conditional on safety and control.

keyExtracts: Mature cell state can be experimentally reprogrammed under defined-factor conditions.
The Human Infra model must distinguish cell identity rewiring from safe subject-level continuity gain.
A path that resets cells too far can become a negative route if identity, cancer or function gates fail.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to introduce cellular reprogramming as a research domain and to require identity-preservation gates.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a claim jumps from iPS induction to human rejuvenation, mark it as unsupported and require partial-reprogramming and clinical safety evidence.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not support whole-organism age reversal, clinical anti-aging use, longevity escape velocity or subject-continuity preservation.
risksAndMisreadings: Pluripotency can be confused with rejuvenation.
Cell-level proof can be confused with organism-level therapy.
Identity erasure can be ignored when only age reset is emphasized.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as the baseline source card for cellular-reprogramming genealogy and safety boundary language.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Pair this card with partial-reprogramming and cancer-risk cards before any positive reprogramming route card is allowed.

sourceIdentity.title: In Vivo Amelioration of Age-Associated Hallmarks by Partial Reprogramming

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to represent partial reprogramming as a preclinical route hypothesis that requires dose, duration, identity and safety gates.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Preclinical improvement signals do not prove human lifespan or healthspan benefit.

modelPosition.stateTransition: Candidate state transition under controlled partial reprogramming exposure.
modelPosition.hazard: Introduces cancer and dysfunction gates as possible negative hazards.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Requires molecular, functional and safety observations.
modelPosition.actionPolicy: No personal action policy; only research route screening.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Cannot set LEV or lifespan timing.
modelPosition.optionValue: May increase future repair route value if identity and safety gates hold.

keyExtracts: Partial reprogramming should be represented as a controlled-window problem rather than a generic rejuvenation slogan.
The positive channel is inseparable from identity loss, tumor and delivery-risk falsifiers.
Human Infra route cards must identify which evidence is animal, cellular, biomarker, functional or clinical.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to define a reprogramming route as candidate-only until clinical endpoint and safety evidence are present.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If dose-duration control, identity retention or tumor-risk evidence is missing, classify the route as cannot-evaluate or negative under safety gates.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not prove human anti-aging therapy, systemic rejuvenation, individual intervention ranking or effective immortality.
risksAndMisreadings: Preclinical hallmarks can be treated as clinical endpoints.
Partial exposure can be presumed safe without delivery and shutdown evidence.
Local or model-organism results can be overgeneralized to whole humans.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a required source for cellular-reprogramming route cards and high-impact C1/C2 field extraction.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Extract dose, duration, model organism, observed endpoints, adverse signals and human-transfer gaps into a dedicated route card.

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to anchor cancer as a core negative-channel and safety-boundary system for any route that increases proliferation, repair or reprogramming pressure.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Cancer mechanism taxonomy does not prove screening or intervention benefit.

modelPosition.stateTransition: Mechanism vocabulary for adverse transitions toward malignant states.
modelPosition.hazard: Supports cancer-risk language but not calibrated Human Infra hazard estimates.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Suggests screening and surveillance variables require benefit-harm review.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Cancer risk can constrain healthspan and survival, but no time estimate is imported.
modelPosition.optionValue: High cancer risk can destroy future option value even when repair signals improve.

keyExtracts: Any growth, regeneration or reprogramming claim needs an explicit cancer-risk channel.
Cancer control is not equivalent to early detection unless outcomes and harms are addressed.
Human Infra should treat tumor risk as an abort or downgrade gate for aggressive maintenance routes.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to require cancer-risk falsifiers for reprogramming, stem-cell and regenerative routes.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a route increases proliferative or identity-changing pressure without cancer-risk governance, downgrade or block the claim.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not support a specific screening protocol, treatment choice, personal cancer-risk estimate or net survival benefit.
risksAndMisreadings: Cancer-hallmark knowledge can be mistaken for cancer-control capability.
Screening can be mistaken for mortality reduction without bias and harm review.
Repair-oriented routes can ignore malignant transformation risk.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a cross-cutting safety source card for C1/C2 route gates.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Pair with screening-bias and clinical endpoint cards before any cancer-control route is promoted.

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source as the method anchor for aggregate survival-curve thinking and censoring-aware visualization boundaries.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Survival method support is not parameter validation.

modelPosition.hazard: Complements hazard thinking by estimating survival functions.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Primary use: lifespan and event-time accounting at aggregate level.
modelPosition.optionValue: Supports visualizing remaining population-level survival, not personal fate.

keyExtracts: Human Infra survival visualizations need censoring-aware aggregate logic.
A survival curve is not an individual death-date prediction.
Any model page using S(t) language must specify population, time origin and event definition.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to anchor aggregate survival curves and prohibit individual date outputs.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a chart infers individual remaining life from aggregate survival language, fail the boundary gate.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not validate a data source, intervention, scenario parameter, NCG value or personal survival estimate.
risksAndMisreadings: Aggregate curves can be read as personal predictions.
Censoring assumptions can be ignored.
Synthetic curves can be mistaken for real calibrated evidence.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a method card for model and Web visualization gates.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Create a survival-visualization checklist covering cohort, time zero, censoring, event and prohibited outputs.

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source as the method anchor for hazard-function and covariate-to-risk language in the Human Infra model contract.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Hazard modeling is not causal proof by itself.

modelPosition.stateVariable: Covariates may represent state variables if measured.
modelPosition.stateTransition: No state transition model unless extended by longitudinal design.
modelPosition.hazard: Primary use: risk-function vocabulary and model position.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Requires covariate definition, time origin and event outcome.
modelPosition.actionPolicy: No action policy without causal design.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Connects risk functions to survival over time.
modelPosition.optionValue: Can express risk gradients that affect future option value if validated.

keyExtracts: The Human Infra chain should place interventions through variables before hazard changes.
Association models cannot be treated as intervention simulators without causal assumptions.
Risk-function language needs explicit covariates, outcome, time origin and validation.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to anchor lambda(t) and covariate-risk model language.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a claim treats a covariate association as do(A) intervention effect, downgrade it to observational association.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not prove causality, individual prediction validity, external calibration or a specific intervention effect.
risksAndMisreadings: Hazard ratios can be overread as causal effects.
Proportional-hazard assumptions can be hidden.
Population-level risk can be overtransferred to personal advice.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a required method card for life-path prediction and hazard-position claims.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Add a hazard-model reporting checklist aligned with causal and prediction-model cards.

sourceIdentity.title: A Framework for Causal Inference From Observational Data

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to anchor the intervention-versus-association boundary and the requirement to emulate a target trial before estimating action effects.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Causal framing does not remove data quality, confounding or ethics constraints.

modelPosition.stateVariable: Defines which baseline and time-varying variables must be explicit.
modelPosition.stateTransition: Can support intervention-state-transition design if estimand fields are complete.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Separates measured history from treatment assignment and outcome.
modelPosition.actionPolicy: Primary method anchor for intervention-policy evaluation.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Requires time zero, follow-up and endpoint horizon.
modelPosition.optionValue: Helps decide whether a route is actionable or only observational.

keyExtracts: Human Infra should ask what trial would answer the intervention question before using observational data.
Eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcome and analysis plan are required for causal claims.
Without a target-trial frame, technology claims should remain association, mechanism or candidate-route claims.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to gate all claims that say a technology or intervention changes lifespan, healthspan, effective time or future option value.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If no intervention, comparator, time zero or endpoint can be specified, mark the route cannot-evaluate for causal effect.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not make weak data causal, does not validate unmeasured confounding control and does not produce personal recommendations.
risksAndMisreadings: Target-trial vocabulary can be used without real data feasibility.
Observational completeness can be mistaken for randomization.
Actionability can be claimed before eligibility and endpoint are specified.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a central field-level card for moving from qualitative routes to quantitative estimands.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Create a reusable target-trial field template for route cards and future model data manifests.

sourceIdentity.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to anchor prediction-model reporting, validation and no-overclaim boundaries for any Human Infra quantitative model page.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Reporting guidance does not certify a model as valid.

modelPosition.stateVariable: Requires explicit predictor and outcome definitions.
modelPosition.hazard: Prediction models may include risk outputs only with validation and calibration.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Primary use: reporting the observation and data pipeline.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Requires horizon and outcome timing if time-dependent predictions exist.
modelPosition.optionValue: Supports transparent uncertainty and model update boundaries.

keyExtracts: Human Infra prediction artifacts must report data, predictors, outcomes, model development, validation and limitations.
A toy model should be explicitly labeled as toy or synthetic and cannot inherit clinical validity from reporting structure.
Prediction governance must keep individual death dates and personal medical advice out of current outputs.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to gate Web model pages, model cards and future data pipeline reporting.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a model lacks validation, calibration, outcome definition or prohibited-output boundary, downgrade it to toy or exploratory status.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not validate the current toy model, NHATS plan, NCG protocol or any clinical prediction.
risksAndMisreadings: Compliance language can be mistaken for model quality.
Transparent reporting can be mistaken for clinical usefulness.
Synthetic outputs can be mistaken for real calibrated predictions.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a reporting-standard card for MODEL-G7 and no-individual-prediction gates.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Create a TRIPOD+AI-aligned model card checklist for Human Infra toy, candidate and real-data model tiers.

sourceCards.oneSentenceUse: Use this source to anchor the value claim that Human Infra cares about real capability to exist, act, learn, recover and choose, not merely biological duration.

humanInfraMapping.safetyBoundary: Normative support does not prove empirical effectiveness.

modelPosition.stateTransition: Conceptual support for how resources convert into action capacity.
modelPosition.observationProcess: Suggests function and option-value observations beyond biomarkers.
modelPosition.actionPolicy: Can shape objective selection, not specific interventions.
modelPosition.timeAccounting: Supports effective time and future choice as value-relevant outputs.
modelPosition.optionValue: Primary value anchor for option value and possibility-space language.

keyExtracts: The project should not reduce effective immortality to biological survival alone.
Resources matter through their conversion into real capabilities and future choices.
Value claims need separate empirical evidence before becoming intervention claims.
sourceCards.supportedUse: Use to explain why effective life, function, agency and future choice are legitimate Human Infra outputs.
sourceCards.falsifierUse: If a route extends time while destroying agency, cognition, function or choice, it fails the capability boundary.
sourceCards.transferBoundary: Does not prove any biological, AI, social or physical route increases capability; it only frames what would count as valuable.
risksAndMisreadings: Normative legitimacy can be mistaken for empirical support.
Capability language can become vague unless tied to variables.
Future choice can be overclaimed without access, adoption and continuity gates.
sourceCards.repositoryAction: Use as a value Source Card connecting HI-CL1/HI-CL3 to measurable function and option-value fields.
sourceCards.nextExtractionStep: Create a capability-to-variable crosswalk for effective time, function, agency, recovery and future option value.

coverageSummary.remainingWork: Extract the remaining 11 anchors, then split domain-level cards for C1/C2 priority claims.

nonClaims: This register does not prove any source is sufficient for an intervention claim.
This register does not permit individual death-date prediction, individual clinical advice, individual lifespan ranking or unvalidated model calibration.
This register does not complete all field-level Source Cards; it is the first extraction slice.
This register is a local traceability gate for research framework maturity, not a scientific literature review substitute.
